questions.q: What were the causes of the disintegration of the Soviet Union?
answer: The Soviet Union, once a mighty superpower, disintegrated in 1991 for several connected reasons.

answer.text: The Soviet economy, based on rigid central planning, had become stagnant and could not produce enough consumer goods. The one-party political system was authoritarian and unaccountable, and the costly arms race with the United States and the long war in Afghanistan drained its resources.

When Mikhail Gorbachev introduced reforms, perestroika to restructure the economy and glasnost to bring openness, they released long-suppressed demands for freedom and reform that the system could not manage or control.
The strongest cause was the rise of nationalism in the various republics, whose people wished to be independent and manage their own affairs.

answer: Together these forces led the Soviet Union to break up into fifteen independent countries, ending the Cold War and leaving the United States as the sole superpower.

questions.q: What were the consequences of the disintegration of the Soviet Union for world politics?

answer.lead: The collapse of the Soviet Union
answer.text: in 1991 ended the Cold War and reshaped world politics profoundly.

list: It ended the bipolar order of two rival superpowers, leaving the United States as the sole superpower
The socialist bloc broke up, and many states turned to democracy and capitalism

answer.lead: The map and balance of power changed.

list: Fifteen new independent countries were born from the former Soviet Union
The ideological contest between capitalism and communism ended, and new powers and conflicts began to shape a changing world order
